You are migrating Java TEST files in the Pathland repo to the v2 authoring surface. You may ONLY edit files matching:
- `lib/java/pathland-render-html/src/test/**`
- `lib/java/pathland-server-core/src/test/**`
- `lib/java/pathland-demo-views/src/test/**`

Do NOT edit main sources or anything else.

The v2 DSL surface (already implemented in `lib/java/pathland-view`):
- Views: `Text.with(t -> t.text("x"))`, `VStack.with(v -> v.alignment(...).spacing(8f)).children(a, b)`, `Grid.with(g -> g.columns(2)).children(a, b)`, `Button.with(b -> b.title("t").action(...))` or `Button.with(b -> b.action(...)).children(label)`, `Slider.with(s -> s.value(sig).in(0f, 100f))`, `Toggle.with(t -> t.isOn(sig))`, etc. All retourn a `ViewBuilder` which IS a `View`.
- `.modifiers(mod, mod2, ...)` — apply modifier values, chainable in any order with `with(...)`/`children(...)`.
- Modifier factories: `Padding.with(p -> p.uniform(16))`, `FontSize.with(s -> s.size(18))`, `ForegroundStyle.with(f -> f.color(color))`, `Background.with(b -> b.color(color))`, `Frame.with(f -> f.width(w).height(h))`, `Border.with(b -> b.color(c).width(w).radius(r))`, `Opacity.with(o -> o.value(v))`, etc. Single-value enum/Font/Style types are modifiers directly: `FontWeight.BOLD`, `Font.system(18f)`, `Font.title2()`, `TextAlignment.CENTER`.

REPLACE these usages in the tests:
1. `view.font(Font.x())` → `view.modifiers(Font.x())`
2. `view.environment(EnvironmentKey, value)` → `view.modifiers(EnvironmentBinding.with(e -> e.key(key).value(value)))` (import `com.pathland.view.EnvironmentBinding`)
3. `view.onPathChange(listener)` → `view.modifiers(PathChange.with(p -> p.listener(listener)))` (import `com.pathland.view.PathChange`)
4. `view.navigate(path)` → `view.modifiers(NavigationIntent.navigate(path))`; `.push`/`.replace` similarly (import `com.pathland.view.router.NavigationIntent`)
5. `view.with(ButtonStyleMod.of(style))` → `view.modifiers(style)`
6. `X.of(...)` for views → `X.with(...)` per the same rules as the main migration (e.g. `Text.of("x")` → `Text.with(t -> t.text("x"))`, `VStack.of(align, spacing, a, b)` → `VStack.with(...).children(a, b)`, `Button.of(title, action)` → `Button.with(b -> b.title(title).action(action))`, `NavigationContainer.of(router)` → `NavigationContainer.with(n -> n.router(router))`, `Slider.of(sig, min, max)` → `Slider.with(s -> s.value(sig).in(min, max))`).
7. `FontWeightMod.of(...)` → the enum value directly; any other `*Mod.of(...)` → the wrapped value.

Import changes needed:
- `com.pathland.view.ButtonStyleMod` → remove; use `BorderedButtonStyle.INSTANCE`/`PlainButtonStyle.INSTANCE` directly as modifier values.

Rules:
- Preserve test *intent* and assertions exactly — only authoring syntax changes. Do not change expected values, count assertions, or rendered-HTML string expectations.
- If a test variable was typed as the concrete class (e.g. `VStack`) but now holds a `ViewBuilder`, change the variable's declared type to `View` (or `var`).
- `View.with(ViewModifier...)` instance method still exists and works on plain `View` values, but PREFER `.modifiers(...)` on builders. When chaining on a plain `View` (not a builder), keep `.with(...)`.
- Do NOT reformat unrelated code.
- Consult `lib/java/pathland-view/src/main/java/com/pathland/view/` class files to confirm config setter names whenever unsure. Never guess.

## Compile verification
`cd lib/java && mvn -o -q -pl pathland-render-html,pathland-server-core,pathland-demo-views -am test-compile`
Fix errors until it compiles. Then run `mvn -o -q -pl pathland-server-core,pathland-render-html,pathland-demo-views test` and ensure all tests pass (note: pathland-render-html tests may require a Rust dylib — if it fails for a missing native lib, report that separately but the compile must be clean).
If any failures are unrelated to your migration (pre-existing), report them.

Report: files changed, any residue you could not migrate, and the test result.

21: /**
22:  * The session delta batcher: merges per-signal frames into one network batch
23:  * (the Java analogue of the Rust transport's {@code Batcher}), rebasing string
24:  * offsets, so a continuous input burst collapses into far fewer WebSocket
25:  * messages instead of overflowing the send queue.
26:  */
27: class DeltaBatcherTest {

31:     @Test
32:     void mergesFramesIntoOneBatchWithRebasedStrings() {
33:         List<byte[]> sent = new ArrayList<>();
34:         // A long flush interval + manual flush keeps the test deterministic.
35:         DeltaBatcher batcher = new DeltaBatcher(60_000, 1_000_000, sent::add);
36: 
37:         // ProtocolFrame 1: SET_TEXT "ab" (offset 0) + a numeric VALUE change.
38:         byte[] strings1 = stringSection("ab");
39:         ProtocolFrame f1 = new ProtocolFrame(List.of(
40:                 new Opcode(Categories.PARAMETER, Commands.Parameter.SET_TEXT, 0, 1, 0, 0),
41:                 new Opcode(Categories.PARAMETER, Commands.Parameter.SET_PROPERTY, 0, 1,
42:                         (ValueTypes.F32 << 16) | PROP_VALUE, Float.floatToIntBits(0.5f))),
43:                 strings1);
44:         // ProtocolFrame 2: SET_TEXT "cd" (its relative offset 0 must rebase past frame 1's section).
45:         byte[] strings2 = stringSection("cd");
46:         ProtocolFrame f2 = new ProtocolFrame(List.of(
47:                 new Opcode(Categories.PARAMETER, Commands.Parameter.SET_TEXT, 0, 2, 0, 0)),
48:                 strings2);
49: 
50:         batcher.append(f1);
51:         batcher.append(f2);
52:         batcher.flush();
53:         batcher.close();
54: 
55:         assertEquals(1, sent.size(), "all frames flush as a single batch");
56:         ProtocolFrame merged = FrameCodec.decodeFrame(sent.get(0));
57:         assertEquals(3, merged.opcodes().size());
58:         // ProtocolFrame 1's SET_TEXT offset stays 0 ("ab"); frame 2's is rebased to 6.
59:         assertEquals("ab", merged.stringAt(0));
60:         assertEquals("cd", merged.stringAt(6));

- `lib/java/pathland-demo-views/src/test/java/com/pathland/demo/SplitNavDemoTest.java`

## What was migrated
- Views `X.of(...)` → `X.with(...)`/`X.children(...)`: `Text`, `Button`, `VStack`, `Toggle`, `Slider`, `Picker` (+`.children`), `ProgressView`, `TextEditor`, `DatePicker`, `Video`, `Audio`, `Image`; bare `Divider.of()` → `Divider.modifiers()`.
- Plain-`View` chaining kept `.with(...)`; builders use `.modifiers(...)`.
- `Button.of(Text.of(sig), action)` → `Button.with(b -> b.action(...)).children(Text.with(...))`.
- `view.font(Font.x())` → `view.modifiers(Font.x())`.
- `ButtonStyleMod.of(style)` + import removed → `view.modifiers(BorderedButtonStyle.INSTANCE)`.
- `AccessibilityRole.of / AccessibilityLabel.of / ScaledToFill.of` modifier values → `.with(...)`/`.with()` (matching the already-migrated main sources).
- `SplitNavDemoTest`: `new SplitNavDemo().environment(key, sig)` → `new SplitNavDemo().with(EnvironmentBinding.with(e -> e.key(key).value(sig)))` (plain composite `View` → `.with`), added the `EnvironmentBinding` import.

## Residue / intentionally kept
- `AccessibilityRole.of(20)` in `HtmlRendererTest` — tests the factory's reserved-code validation, not authoring.
- `Event.navigate(...)` (transport event) and a doc comment mentioning `.navigate(...)` — not DSL authoring.

## Test result
`mvn -o -pl pathland-server-core,pathland-render-html,pathland-demo-views test` → **BUILD SUCCESS**, 75 tests, 0 failures/errors (render-html 11, server-core 33, demo-views 31). The Rust dylib was present, so the render-html shim tests ran.

- `pathland-view/src/test/java/com/pathland/view/LabelTest.java` and `.../router/RouterTest.java` call removed main APIs (`NavigationContainer.of(...)`, `NavigationLink.of(...)`).

None of those errors are in the three migration modules; I did not touch `pathland-view` (not in scope).
